1 These criminal appeals under Section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act have been preferred by the appellants with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection orders dated 20.09.2023 and 22.08.2023 passed by learned Special Judge SC/ST (P.A.) Act, Firozabad in Bail Application Nos. 3134 of 2023 and 2922 of 2023, arising out of Case Crime No. 540 of 2023, under Sections 366, 376-D I.P.C. and Section 3 (2) V of SC/ST (P.A.) Act,
Police Station Tundla, District Firozabad.
There is allegation against the named accused Ajay that on 15.07.2023 at around 11.30 am, when the daughter of the informant was going to her college, he met her and enticed her away.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the appellants are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case.
The age of the victim as per High School Certificate is 19 years.
The victim was having friendship with appellant Ajay.
The other appellant Vineet Kumar was not named in the F.I.R. and his name disclosed by the victim during her statement recorded under Section 161Cr.P.C.

Initially the victim refused to undergo for her medical examination but later on she moved an application for conducting her medical examination stating that she was under pressure,
therefore, she refused to undergo for her medical examination earlier.
During her medical examination no internal or external injury was noted.
During her statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., she did not make any allegations against the appellants that they established physical relation with her.
It is further submitted that photographs and whats-app chat brought on record which demonstrate that victim was consenting party and she was cordial relation with the appellant Ajay.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the appellants that there is no chance of the appellants fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The appellants do not have any criminal history to their credit.
The appellants are languishing in jail since 02.08.2023 and in case they are released on bail, they will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the early disposal of the case.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. assisted by learned counsel for the informant opposed the aforesaid prayer and submitted that during statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. victim has made certain allegations against the appellants.
whats-app chat has not value and no certificate under Section 65 (b) of Evidence Act is brought on record.
However, they could not dispute the aforesaid factual aspects of the matter.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, this Court is of the view that the appellants have made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail applications.
The impugned orders suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same are liable to be set-aside and the appeals are liable to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeals are allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant, namely, Ajay Kumar and Vineet Kumar involved in the above Case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Ajay Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70475505/
2 court concerned subject to following conditions.

entities.text: Ajay Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The appellants will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The appellants will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The appellants will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence are exempted.
(iv) The appellants shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which they are suspected.

(v) The appellants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
